subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A coal sample (proximate analysis) has 5% moisture, 25% volatile matter and 8% ash. Its fixed carbon is:
solution: Fixed C = 100 − (moisture + VM + ash) = 100 − (5+25+8) = 62%.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Groundwater recharge can occur through which combination of natural and artificial processes?
options: Natural (rainfall infiltration) and artificial (recharge wells, ponds, check dams)
Occurs only through the direct infiltration of seasonal rainfall into the ground surface
Results only from artificial structures built for the purpose
Happens only where sea water intrudes into the coastal aquifer
solution: Recharge: ~10-20% of rainfall in alluvial areas. Artificial: managed aquifer recharge (MAR).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What is the approximate specific gravity of gold found in its native form?
solution: Gold (Au) — SG 15-19. Heavy mineral. Placer deposits.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which option correctly describes the cross-profile of a valley produced by fluvial incision during the youthful stage?
options: Valley with a wide flat floor built of alluvial sediment
Broad valley with steep walls and a flat floor cut by ice
Fluvial incision (youthful stage). Steep sides, narrow floor
Channel pattern with multiple bars and rapidly shifting unstable channels
solution: V-shaped: downcutting > lateral erosion. Rapids and waterfalls common.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which spaceborne sensor carries the MSI instrument with 13 bands, a 5-day revisit, and is suited to vegetation and agriculture?
options: The OLI sensor, with 9 spectral bands at 30m resolution and a 16-day revisit period
The MODIS sensor, with 36 spectral bands at 250-1000m for daily global coverage
The ETM+ sensor, with 8 bands, a 15m panchromatic band, and a 16-day revisit period
MSI (13 bands, 10-60m). 5-day revisit. 290km swath. Vegetation, agriculture

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What type of material is most suitable for rip-rap used in erosion protection?
options: Soft, easily weathered sandstone placed as rounded cobbles without any proper bedding layer
Silty clay compacted in layers to form a smooth impermeable face
Uniform rounded boulders of low specific gravity dumped loosely
Hard, durable rock (granite, basalt). Angular, well-graded. Weight: W₅₀ design
solution: Riprap: properly sized. Bedding layer underneath. Filter layer prevents piping.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What is a very coarse-grained igneous rock with crystals over 2.5 cm, enriched in rare elements?
options: Very coarse-grained igneous rock (>2.5 cm crystals). Enriched in rare elements
Fine-grained volcanic rock formed by the rapid quenching of a felsic magma at the surface
Glassy rock produced by instantaneous chilling of rhyolitic lava
Medium-grained plutonic rock with crystals between one and five mm
solution: Pegmatite: high volatile content (H2O, F, Cl). Source of Li, Be, Cs, rare earths.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What is the stratigraphic relation, lithology, and age of the Kurnool Group in peninsular India?
options: Archean greenstone succession conformably beneath the oldest Dharwar schist belt
Overlies Cuddapah unconformably. Diamictite, limestone, quartzite. Neoproterozoic
Cretaceous marine shelf sequence with prolific hydrocarbon source rocks in the Kutch basin
Mesozoic Gondwana coal measures overlying the Archean basement in the Damodar valley
solution: Kurnool: Banganapalle quartzite (diamond-bearing). Owk shale. Narji limestone.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: How is phosphorite, a sedimentary rock rich in phosphate minerals, defined?
options: Metamorphic rock dominated by quartz and feldspar formed at high temperature
Sedimentary rock >50% phosphate minerals (apatite). Upwelling zones
Igneous rock composed chiefly of olivine, pyroxene and calcium plagioclase
Deep-sea rock made almost entirely of biogenic silica from radiolarian tests
solution: Phosphorite: marine sediments, Peru-Chile, Morocco. Phosphorus fertilizer. Guano.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Serpentinite forms by the alteration of ultramafic rocks and is notorious for which characteristic?
options: Carbonate rock formed by metamorphism of pure limestone and dolomite strata
Felsic rock composed mainly of quartz, alkali feldspar and mica minerals that shows foliation
Evaporite sequence deposited in arid restricted marine basins and coastal lagoons
Alteration of ultramafic rock (olivine→serpentine). Slip planes — landslide hazard
solution: Serpentinite: tectonic melanges. Asbestos minerals (chrysotile). Weak, slippery.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) frequency affects:
options: Depth penetration and resolution trade-off
Only horizontal resolution at the cost of depth
Depth and resolution both fixed by the antenna
Only the colour contrast of the recorded radargram
solution: GPR: higher freq = better resolution but less depth. Lower freq = more depth but less resolution. 10 MHz - 2 GHz.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: An ore body of 5 Mt has an average metal grade of 3%. The contained metal is about:
options: 15 kt
300 kt
75 kt
150 kt
solution: Metal = tonnage × grade = 5 Mt × 3% = 150 thousand tonnes (kt).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A coal sample (proximate analysis) has 8% moisture, 30% volatile matter and 15% ash. Its fixed carbon is:
solution: Fixed C = 100 − (moisture + VM + ash) = 100 − (8+30+15) = 47%.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which term describes minerals having the same chemical composition but different crystal structures?
options: Two minerals having different chemical compositions and different crystal structures are polymorphs
Same composition, different crystal structure (e.g., graphite/diamond, calcite/aragonite)
Same composition and same structure forming in different habits
Same structure containing different chemical compositions
solution: Polymorphs: diamond (cubic) and graphite (hexagonal) — both C.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which material property, its resistance to temperature change, is mapped remotely using day-night temperature differences?
options: Resistance to temperature change. High for wet/dense materials. Day-night ΔT for mapping
The rate of heat flow, which depends only upon the surface colour of the material that is involved
A uniform material property of the ground that is identical for all rock types present
Low for wet and dense materials such as water, while high for dry loose sand
solution: Thermal inertia: √(ρ·k·C_p). Quartz: high. Water: very high. Dry sand: low. Used in geology.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Rare earth element (REE) patterns: chondrite-normalized. LREE enrichment (La/Sm)_N > 1 indicates:
options: Primitive mantle source that has undergone no prior melt extraction
Enriched mantle source or crustal contamination
Depleted source such as the mantle beneath normal mid-ocean ridges
Source in which no fractionation of rare earth elements has occurred
solution: LREE enriched: OIB, arc, continental. LREE depleted: N-MORB. Chondrite normalized: divides by chondrite values.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which index minerals mark increasing metamorphic grade in pelitic rocks, and in what order do they appear?
options: A random sequence that has no systematic relation to the metamorphic grade
Chlorite → biotite → garnet → staurolite → kyanite → sillimanite (increasing grade)
Reverse order: sillimanite → kyanite → staurolite → garnet → biotite with increasing grade
An identical assemblage at every grade throughout the metamorphic terrane
solution: Barrovian index minerals: each stable in specific P-T window. Increasing grade = higher T/P.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A coal seam covers 5 km², is 3 m thick, with density 1.4 t/m³. The in-situ reserve is about:
options: 42 Mt
15 Mt
21 Mt
solution: Reserve = area×thickness×density = 5×10⁶ m²×3 m×1.4 t/m³ ≈ 21 Mt.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: GPS positioning: code-phase accuracy vs carrier-phase:
options: Code-phase: ~1-10m. Carrier-phase: ~1cm (RTK)
Code-phase: ~1cm. Carrier-phase: ~1-10m with RTK
Code and carrier-phase have identical accuracies
Carrier-phase is less accurate than code-phase
solution: Carrier-phase: millimeter precision. RTK: real-time kinematic. Static: post-processed.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which Precambrian rock type best exemplifies iron-rich sedimentary rocks, and what is its composition?
options: A Phanerozoic deposit of iron oxides formed mostly during the Triassic period, with chert bands absent
A sedimentary sequence rich in iron deposited mainly during the Cenozoic era
Banded Iron Formation (BIF): Precambrian, chert + iron oxides (hematite, magnetite)
Modern iron-rich muds accumulating in deep anoxic ocean basins at present
solution: BIF: major Fe ore. Algoma-type (volcanic) vs Superior-type (cratonic). Banded: microbands.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Steep-sided limestone towers separated by flat plains, also known as peak clusters, characterise which karst landform assemblage?
options: Steep-sided limestone towers separated by plains. Peak cluster
Cone karst consists of conical limestone hills with sinkholes between them
Landform built up by repeated eruptions of lava, ash and other volcanic material
Landform produced by erosion of rock beneath glacier ice
solution: Tower karst: Guilin (China), Ha Long Bay. Fenglin: isolated towers. Fengcong: connected peaks.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What is the origin and composition of deep marine siliceous rocks such as chert and radiolarite?
options: Fluvial gravels with rounded quartz pebbles and chert fragments, but with no siliceous biogenic component at all
Deep marine siliceous ooze. Radiolaria, diatoms, sponge spicules. Recrystallized to microcrystalline quartz
Deltaic sands with heavy mineral placers and abundant carbonaceous plant debris
Shallow-water carbonate sands with ooids and bioclasts, but without any silica present
solution: Chert: SiO₂. Radiolarite: radiolarian tests. Bedded or nodular chert in limestone.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which of the following correctly describes a pediment at the base of a mountain front?
options: Surface built entirely of sediment deposited by rivers at the mountain front forming a wide depositional plain
Very steep cliff face cut into resistant bedrock at the mountain edge by river undercutting
Gently sloping erosional surface at mountain base. Bedrock with thin alluvium
Flat floor of a valley filled with thick alluvial sediment deposited by river flood events
solution: Pediment: desert piedmont. Pediplain: coalescing pediments. Parallel retreat of slopes (Penck).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Using Mohs hardness, which comparison is correct?
options: Quartz (7) scratches feldspar (6)
Calcite (3) scratches quartz (7)
Feldspar (6) scratches corundum (9)
Talc (1) scratches gypsum (2)
solution: A harder mineral scratches a softer one; quartz (7) > feldspar (6).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Stream power law: Ω = ρgQS. Incision rate E = K·Ω^m·S^n. For m=1, n=1:
options: E ∝ Q²
E ∝ S²
E ∝ Q·S²
E ∝ Q·S
solution: Stream power: erosion rate depends on discharge and slope. m≈1, n≈1 (simplified.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Mohr circle for stress: center = (σ₁+σ₃)/2, radius = (σ₁-σ₃)/2. For σ₁=100MPa, σ₃=40MPa:
options: Center=50MPa, radius=50MPa
Center=70MPa, radius=30MPa
Center=70MPa, radius=60MPa
Center=40MPa, radius=30MPa

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: On a stereonet, the β-axis of a fold is determined by the intersection of which features?
options: The average of the strike directions of all measured beds on the stereonet
The pole to the axial plane plotted as a single point on the stereonet
The maximum concentration of poles to bedding contoured on the projection
Intersection of great circles through two fold limbs
solution: β-axis: intersection of two great circles representing limb orientations. π-diagram: poles to limbs.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Storativity S of an aquifer is defined as the volume of water:
options: The total volume of water that an aquifer can store above the level of the water table
Volume released per unit area per unit head drop. Confined: elastic storage (~10⁻⁵-10⁻³)
The rate at which groundwater flows across a unit cross sectional area of the aquifer formation
The ratio of the saturated aquifer thickness to the hydraulic conductivity value
solution: S = Ss·b (specific storage × thickness). Unconfined: S ~ S_y (specific yield, 0.1-0.3).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A coal sample (proximate analysis) has 8% moisture, 35% volatile matter and 20% ash. Its fixed carbon is:
solution: Fixed C = 100 − (moisture + VM + ash) = 100 − (8+35+20) = 37%.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A dipping coal seam outcrops over a horizontal width of 100 m on flat ground and dips at 20°. Its true thickness is about:
solution: True thickness = horizontal width × sin(dip) = 100×sin20° ≈ 34.2 m.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: To which structural class of silicates does the mineral muscovite belong?
options: Tectosilicates (framework silicates)
Sorosilicates (paired tetrahedra)
Phyllosilicates (sheet silicates)
Nesosilicates (independent tetrahedra)
solution: Muscovite — white mica. Good electrical insulator. Used in capacitors.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: An aquifer (K = 50 m/day) of cross-section 500 m² has a hydraulic gradient of 0.02. The groundwater discharge is about:
options: 500 m³/day
250 m³/day
25000 m³/day
1000 m³/day

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A coal seam covers 1 km², is 3 m thick, with density 1.4 t/m³. The in-situ reserve is about:
options: 8.4 Mt
2.1 Mt
3 Mt
4.2 Mt
solution: Reserve = area×thickness×density = 1×10⁶ m²×3 m×1.4 t/m³ ≈ 4.2 Mt.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Radiometric dating works because a radioactive parent isotope decays to a daughter at a rate set by its:
options: Depth of burial below the Earth's surface
Constant half-life
Pressure prevailing at the site of formation
Temperature of the surrounding environment
solution: Decay is exponential with a fixed half-life, so the parent/daughter ratio gives an absolute age.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: An aquifer (K = 10 m/day) of cross-section 200 m² has a hydraulic gradient of 0.01. The groundwater discharge is about:
options: 2000 m³/day
40 m³/day
10 m³/day
20 m³/day

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Granulite is a high-grade metamorphic rock distinguished by the presence of which mineral assemblage?
options: High-grade metamorphic. No hydrous minerals (pyroxene + feldspar + garnet)
Low-grade metamorphic rock rich in chlorite, muscovite, biotite and quartz minerals
Contact metamorphic hornfels formed adjacent to a large igneous intrusion
Mica-rich rock with a strong foliation formed at low to medium grade
solution: Granulite: dry metamorphism. H2O absent. Pyroxene stable, biotite unstable.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A 3 m seam over 6 km² (density 1.4 t/m³) has a recovery factor of 0.75. The mineable reserve is about:
solution: Mineable = area×thickness×density×recovery = 6M m²×3×1.4×0.75 ≈ 18.9 Mt.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What is chalk composed of, and what are its characteristic physical properties?
options: Coarse-grained limestone with abundant large shelly fossils throughout
Dolomitic limestone formed by magnesium replacement of calcium
Evaporite deposit of halite and gypsum from a restricted basin
Microscopic coccoliths (marine algae). Soft, white
solution: Chalk: White Cliffs of Dover. Pure CaCO3. Used in cement, lime.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Pencil cleavage, which yields slender pencil-shaped rock fragments in deformed rocks, develops under which condition?
options: Two cleavages intersect at high angle
A single cleavage overprints undeformed strata
Primary bedding is preserved without any strain
Shear stress rotates pre-existing fold hinges
solution: Pencil cleavage: intersection of two cleavages at ~90°. Rock breaks into pencil-shaped fragments. Common in fold hinges.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A coal sample (proximate analysis) has 8% moisture, 25% volatile matter and 20% ash. Its fixed carbon is:
solution: Fixed C = 100 − (moisture + VM + ash) = 100 − (8+25+20) = 47%.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: An aquitard is a geological unit that yields little water to wells but may store and transmit water slowly; such a unit is:
options: A coarse grained unit that yields large quantities of water very easily to pumping wells
A unit that only stores water and never transmits it to wells during pumping
Low permeability unit (silt, clay, shale). Poor yield, may store/transmit slowly
A highly permeable formation such as clean gravel or heavily fractured rock of granite
solution: Aquitard: retards vertical flow. Leakage through aquitard → aquitard-aquifer system.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A mineral that effervesces (fizzes) when dilute hydrochloric acid is applied is:
options: Feldspar
Quartz
Calcite
Garnet
solution: Calcite (CaCO₃) reacts with dilute HCl, releasing CO₂ — a standard field test.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which intrusive igneous body is concordant and domes the overlying strata?
options: Concordant intrusion that domes overlying strata
Discordant intrusion that cross-cuts the enclosing country rocks
Concordant intrusion that forms broad flat layers of basaltic composition
Narrow cylindrical body filling the feeder conduit of a volcano
solution: Laccolith: mushroom-shaped. Overlying beds arched upward.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: The Moho discontinuity, marking the base of the crust, lies at what depths beneath oceanic and continental crust?
options: 100 km. A uniform depth beneath oceans and continents, coincident with the top of the asthenosphere
2 km. The shallow depth at which the Conrad surface truncates the continental upper crust
~5-10 km (oceanic), ~30-50 km (continental). Base of crust. Seismic P-wave jump ~6.7→8.1 km/s
10 km everywhere. S-wave velocities drop sharply below this universal crustal base
solution: Moho: crust-mantle boundary. Defined by Vp. Faster in mafic lower crust.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: An aquiclude is a saturated geological unit that is essentially impermeable and yields no significant water; it is typically composed of:
options: Impermeable unit (clay, massive shale). No significant yield
A saturated permeable unit that yields useful quantities of water
A fractured rock unit with good storage and moderate transmission
A coarse sand bed that transmits water with very little resistance
solution: Aquiclude: prevents flow. Confining layer in confined aquifer.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: How are rock units classified and ranked in the discipline of lithostratigraphy?
options: Division of rocks based only on their structural and tectonic features
Subdivision of the rock column on the basis of measured absolute ages
Correlation of strata on the basis of their contained fossil content
Rock units based on lithology (Formation, Member, Group)
solution: Formation: mappable unit. Member: subdivision. Group: several formations.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Unconformity-related uranium deposits, like those in the Athabasca Basin, are characterized by what features?
options: Placer accumulation of heavy radioactive minerals in mature beach sands
Sandstone-hosted roll-front uranium precipitated along redox boundaries between oxidized and reduced aquifer zones
Volcanic-hosted uranium associated with peralkaline rhyolite calderas
Athabasca Basin (Canada). High grade (>1% U₃O₈). Basement + sandstone. U/Pb age ~1.5 Ga
solution: Unconformity: massive U within altered basement. Cigar Lake, McArthur River.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What is the relative duration of the Precambrian, Paleozoic, Mesozoic, and Cenozoic in the geological time scale?
options: All eras are of equal duration across the entire geological time scale of the Earth history
Precambrian is the shortest interval, covering less than 10% of Earth's recorded geological history
Precambrian (88%), Paleozoic (545-251 Ma), Mesozoic (251-66 Ma), Cenozoic (66 Ma-present)
Cenozoic is the longest era, spanning nearly half of the total Earth history span recorded
solution: Hadean, Archean, Proterozoic (Precambrian). Phanerozoic: Paleo-Meso-Cenozoic.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: The magnetotelluric (MT) method uses what natural source field, and which parameter is measured from it?
options: Controlled dc current injected to map resistivity at shallow depth
Seismic waves generated by an airgun source to image deep crustal reflectors
Gravity measurements reduced for terrain to model the Moho depth beneath a basin
Natural EM field (lightning, solar wind). Measures impedance Z = E/H
solution: MT: deep crustal imaging. Low frequency → deep. Resistivity model. MTZ: mid-crustal conductor.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: On the Mohs scale of mineral hardness, what hardness value does the mineral corundum have?
solution: Corundum (Al2O3) — 9. Sapphire and ruby are gem varieties.
